greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is the King of all creation, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the King who comes to us in love. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you invite us to be faithful with the gifts we have received. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you call us to trust in your promise of eternal life. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Holy, holy, holy Lord, mighty God!
homily:
Imagine, if you will, the vast, silent expanse of the sky. Think of the way an airplane—perhaps one of those Boeing 737s that Benjamin loved to watch—looks against the infinite blue. From the ground, it seems small, almost fragile, yet it is held by the physics of the air and the steady hand of the pilot. It has a destination. It has a path. It is moving toward a place it cannot yet see, trusting in the instruments and the air beneath its wings. There is a quiet majesty in that movement, a sense of purpose that defies the limitations of gravity. 

In our first reading today, John is caught up in the spirit and sees a door standing open in heaven. He sees a throne, and around that throne, the four living creatures, covered with eyes, singing without ceasing: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God almighty.' This is the destination of every human life. It is not just a place; it is a presence. It is the reality behind the veil of our daily, often heavy, existence. We live our lives down here, navigating the clouds and the storms, but there is an open door at the end of the journey. There is a throne of grace where the King sits, and he is the one who created all things. He is the one who, by his will, brought Benjamin into being, and he is the one who holds him now in the eternal sunlight of his presence.

I want you to hold onto this image: the open door. It is the image of a life that has reached its true home. It is the image of Benjamin Vo. Think of the way Benjamin lived—always reaching, always learning, always curious. He was a boy who looked at the world as if it were a vast map waiting to be explored. Whether he was coding a new game on GitHub, discussing the complexities of cloud infrastructure, or giggling as he imagined the future of 'con chim airlines,' he was a boy who understood that life is meant to be lived with a sense of wonder. He was a boy who was always looking up, always looking forward, always seeking to understand the mechanics of the world around him. He lived with a bright, open-hearted intelligence that was, in its own way, a constant act of praise.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: it has been five months since he went home to God. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know that the calendar moves forward, but the heart often pauses in the quiet spaces where his laughter used to echo. We know the sharp, sudden ache that comes when you see something he would have loved—a new technological advancement, a bird in flight, or a moment of family joy—and the silence that follows is profound. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the waves of sorrow that ambush you in the middle of an ordinary day. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer. Your tears are the language of a love that is still very much alive.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus tells the parable of the nobleman who gives his servants coins to trade. He is teaching them about the nature of the Kingdom—that it is not something we wait for passively, but something we participate in with our whole lives. He asks for faithfulness. He asks that we use the gifts we have been given, that we share the light we have been entrusted with. Benjamin did exactly this. Think of that remarkable moment when he, at just fifteen years old and completely unprompted, told his parents he was willing to give up his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William. He didn't need to break it open; the offer itself revealed the magnificent generosity of his soul. He was a boy whose heart was already sized for eternity. He was a boy who knew that the true wealth of life is not what we keep, but what we are willing to offer for the sake of those we love. That love is the talent that does not die; it is the gift that multiplies in the eyes of God.

This is the hinge of the mystery. We think our lives are small, limited by time and space. But in the eyes of the King, every act of love is a coin invested in the Kingdom. Every smile, every giggle about an imaginary airline, every moment of empathy for a loved one—these are the things that endure. They are the currency of heaven. Benjamin’s life was not a brief flicker; it was a fire that continues to burn in the hearts of those who knew him. Think of the 'Well of Love' in Cà Mau, that clean water flowing in his name, bringing life to those who were thirsty. That is the work of a life that continues to bear fruit. That is the way Benjamin’s kindness ripples out into the world, touching the lives of people he never met, in a place he may never have walked. His life continues to trade in the currency of love, and the interest on that investment is eternal.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the shared laughter, the way you both navigated the world together. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart.

We hear in the Psalm today: 'Praise him for his mighty deeds, praise him for his sovereign majesty.' This is the turn of the heart. The blessing of the Lord is not that we will never suffer, but that we will never be abandoned in our suffering. Benjamin is now resting in that promise. He is dwelling in the land of the living, fully alive, fully healed, and fully embraced by the Father. He is not a memory tucked away in a photo album; he is a living soul in the Banquet of Heaven, standing alongside kindred spirits, watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected. Think of the dream Alan had, where Ben and his dad stood outside room 419, and Ben said with that earnest voice, 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết... Không sao đâu, con sẽ dõi theo ba mẹ.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was the assurance that he has passed every test, that he is whole, and that he is watching over you with a smile. He is the one who has already crossed the threshold into the light, and he is cheering you on.

There is a peace that comes from knowing that we are held. It is not a peace that takes away the pain overnight, but it is a peace that keeps us from being destroyed by it. It is the peace of knowing that Benjamin is waiting. He is waiting in the light, waiting in the place where there is no more struggling, only the clear, bright presence of God. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain. He is a light in the world, and he is shining for you. He is home. And because he is home, you are never truly lost. He is holding the key to that reunion, and he is waiting for the day when the family of four is whole again in the house of the Father.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
petitions: For Benjamin Vo and all who have died, that they may rest forever in the light of Christ and join the saints in the banquet of heaven, we pray to the Lord.
For all who grieve, especially Benjamin's parents and his brother Ryan, that God may console them with His presence and give them the strength and hope to continue their journey, we pray to the Lord.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of His face shine upon you always. Go in peace.
standing_petitions: For a boy named Ben and all who have died, that they rest in the light of Christ.
For all who grieve, that God console them and give them hope.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
I, John, had a vision of an open door to heaven,
and I heard the trumpetlike voice
that had spoken to me before, saying,
“Come up here and I will show you what must happen afterwards.”
At once I was caught up in spirit.
A throne was there in heaven, and on the throne sat one
whose appearance sparkled like jasper and carnelian.
Around the throne was a halo as brilliant as an emerald.
Surrounding the throne I saw twenty-four other thrones
on which twenty-four elders sat,
dressed in white garments and with gold crowns on their heads.
From the throne came flashes of lightning,
rumblings, and peals of thunder.
Seven flaming torches burned in front of the throne,
which are the seven spirits of God.
In front of the throne was something that resembled
a sea of glass like crystal.In the center and around the throne,
there were four living creatures
covered with eyes in front and in back.
The first creature resembled a lion, the second was like a calf,
the third had a face like that of a man,
and the fourth looked like an eagle in flight.
The four living creatures, each of them with six wings,
were covered with eyes inside and out.
Day and night they do not stop exclaiming:
“Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God almighty,
who was, and who is, and who is to come.”
Whenever the living creatures give glory and honor and thanks
to the one who sits on the throne, who lives forever and ever,
the twenty-four elders fall down
before the one who sits on the throne
and worship him, who lives forever and ever.
They throw down their crowns before the throne, exclaiming:“Worthy are you, Lord our God,
to receive glory and honor and power,
for you created all things;
because of your will they came to be and were created.”

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R.    (1b) Holy, holy, holy Lord, mighty God!
Praise the LORD in his sanctuary,
praise him in the firmament of his strength.
Praise him for his mighty deeds,
praise him for his sovereign majesty.
R.    Holy, holy, holy Lord, mighty God!
Praise him with the blast of the trumpet,
praise him with lyre and harp,
Praise him with timbrel and dance,
praise him with strings and pipe.
R.    Holy, holy, holy Lord, mighty God!
Praise him with sounding cymbals,
praise him with clanging cymbals.
Let everything that has breath
praise the LORD! Alleluia.
R.    Holy, holy, holy Lord, mighty God!

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
While people were listening to Jesus speak,
he proceeded to tell a parable because he was near Jerusalem
and they thought that the Kingdom of God
would appear there immediately.
So he said,
“A nobleman went off to a distant country
to obtain the kingship for himself and then to return.
He called ten of his servants and gave them ten gold coins
and told them, ‘Engage in trade with these until I return.’
His fellow citizens, however, despised him
and sent a delegation after him to announce,
‘We do not want this man to be our king.’
But when he returned after obtaining the kingship,
he had the servants called, to whom he had given the money,
to learn what they had gained by trading.
The first came forward and said,
‘Sir, your gold coin has earned ten additional ones.’
He replied, ‘Well done, good servant!
You have been faithful in this very small matter;
take charge of ten cities.’
Then the second came and reported,
‘Your gold coin, sir, has earned five more.’
And to this servant too he said,
‘You, take charge of five cities.’
Then the other servant came and said,
‘Sir, here is your gold coin;
I kept it stored away in a handkerchief,
for I was afraid of you, because you are a demanding man;
you take up what you did not lay down
and you harvest what you did not plant.’
He said to him,
‘With your own words I shall condemn you,
you wicked servant.
You knew I was a demanding man,
taking up what I did not lay down
and harvesting what I did not plant;
why did you not put my money in a bank?
Then on my return I would have collected it with interest.’
And to those standing by he said,
‘Take the gold coin from him
and give it to the servant who has ten.’
But they said to him,
‘Sir, he has ten gold coins.’
He replied, ‘I tell you,
to everyone who has, more will be given,
but from the one who has not,
even what he has will be taken away.
Now as for those enemies of mine who did not want me as their king,
bring them here and slay them before me.’”After he had said this,
he proceeded on his journey up to Jerusalem.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.
Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
